# Wind Turbine OEMs and Renewables — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global wind turbine OEMs across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Vestas Wind Systems | VWS.CO |
| 2 | Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy (Siemens Energy) | ENR.DE |
| 3 | GE Vernova | GEV |
| 4 | Nordex SE | NDX1.DE |
| 5 | Goldwind Science & Technology | 002202.SZ |
| 6 | Envision Energy | (Private) |
| 7 | Mingyang Smart Energy | 601615.SS |
| 8 | Suzlon Energy | SUZLON.NS |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. FY2024 Pure-Play Wind Turbine Revenue — Reconstruction**
For each entity, reconstruct FY2024 pure-play wind turbine equipment revenue (USD millions) by stripping out service/O&M, grid solutions (GEV), gas/power, and other non-turbine businesses. For Siemens Gamesa, isolate the Wind segment within Siemens Energy and flag any intercompany eliminations with the parent. For Envision (private), triangulate revenue from disclosed MW shipments × ASP benchmarks derived from listed Chinese peers; state ASP assumption explicitly. Note reporting currency and FX conversion date.

**Q2. Cumulative Installed Base — Vintage Decomposition**
Decompose cumulative global installed wind capacity (GW) as of YE2024 into three vintages — pre-2015, 2015-2020, and 2021-2024 — separating onshore vs offshore in each cohort. The three vintages must sum to total cumulative GW. Where OEM self-disclosure diverges from BloombergNEF or Wood Mackenzie by more than 5%, identify the source used and explain the divergence (e.g., repowered units, decommissioned fleet treatment).

**Q3. Book-to-Bill and Backlog Coverage**
For each OEM, compute (a) FY2024 book-to-bill ratio = order intake ÷ wind segment revenue, and (b) backlog coverage in years = end-of-period firm backlog ÷ trailing 12-month wind revenue. Express both to one decimal place and rank the top-3 highest book-to-bill. Identify which two OEMs have the most front-loaded vs back-loaded delivery profile based on disclosed backlog scheduling.

**Q4. FY2024 Wind EBIT Margin — YoY Bridge**
Bridge each OEM's wind-segment EBIT margin from FY2023 to FY2024 by decomposing the YoY change into five components: (a) warranty/quality charges, (b) pricing, (c) raw-material/logistics, (d) FX, (e) volume/mix. The five components must sum to total YoY margin change in basis points. Where only group-level margin is available (Suzlon, Envision), state explicitly and use closest reported proxy. Counterfactual: if Siemens Gamesa's warranty/quality run-rate normalized to Vestas's level, what would FY2024 segment EBIT margin have been?

**Q5. Flagship Turbine — Swept Area per MW**
For each OEM's largest flagship turbine, compute swept-area-per-MW = π(rotor diameter/2)² ÷ rated MW, expressed in m²/MW. Classify status as "prototype installed," "serial production," or "announced/roadmap" — only the latter two count toward "commercially available." Provide rotor diameter, rated MW, and intended market (onshore/offshore). Rank the top-3 largest swept-area-per-MW values.

**Q6. R&D Intensity and Per-MW R&D**
For each OEM, report (a) 3-year R&D CAGR FY2022→FY2024, (b) FY2024 R&D intensity (% of revenue), and (c) R&D-per-MW-shipped (USD thousands per MW). Identify capitalized vs expensed R&D treatment and flag IFRS vs US GAAP differences (notably GE Vernova). Rank the top-3 by R&D-per-MW-shipped.

**Q7. Productivity — Revenue and MW per FTE**
Retrieve total FTE headcount as of YE2024 (or fiscal year-end). Compute (a) revenue-per-FTE (USD thousands) and (b) MW-shipped-per-FTE for each OEM. For GE Vernova, isolate Wind segment FTEs from total Vernova headcount and disclose the allocation methodology used. Rank the top-3 most productive OEMs on each metric.

**Q8. Corporate Restructuring Since 2015 — Strategic Rationale**
For each OEM, identify the most recent corporate restructuring event (spinoff, merger, carve-out, delisting, or acquisition) since 2015, the date completed, and the strategic rationale disclosed by management at the time. Where multiple events occurred (e.g., Siemens Gamesa 2017 merger then 2023 delisting; GE Vernova April 2024 spinoff), document the sequence and identify which event most materially affected current segment-reporting structure.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1 — FY2024 Pure-Play Wind Turbine Equipment Revenue (Reconstruction)

**Methodology.** For each issuer I start from audited segment disclosure, subtract Service/O&M and any non-turbine activities (grid, gas, project EPC margin where separable, foundry/forging, wind-farm development/asset sales), and convert to USD at the **2024 IRS yearly average reference rate** unless an issuer reports under a non-calendar fiscal year (Siemens Energy: Oct-2023 → Sept-2024; Suzlon: April-2023 → March-2024). Where a clean "equipment-only" line is not reported, I keep the closest published "Power Solutions / Projects / WTG" line and note the residual EPC content. For Envision I triangulate from disclosed MW shipments × Chinese-peer ASP. Source tiers: **T1** = audited annual report / 20-F / 10-K; **T2** = earnings release or investor presentation; **T3** = trade-press / BNEF / Wood Mac; **T4** = analyst triangulation/ND-estimate.

### Narrative & key reconciliation notes

**Vestas (#1).** Vestas reports two segments — Power Solutions (PS) and Service. PS already excludes O&M, so it is the cleanest "pure-play" line in the peer group. The only contamination is the EPC margin embedded in some balance-of-plant project scope (Vestas does not separately quantify EPC vs equipment within PS). I therefore present a $14.2 bn point with a $13.7–14.8 bn interval.

**Siemens Gamesa / Siemens Energy (#2).** Siemens Energy presents Wind as one of four segments. Within Wind, SGRE Service revenue (~€2.0 bn FY24) is disclosed in the SGRE legacy disclosures and management commentary but **not** broken out as a separate sub-segment line in the parent 20-F equivalent; I rely on SGRE's last stand-alone FY22 disclosure scaled by service-fleet growth. **Intercompany eliminations** with the parent are disclosed at the SE consolidation level (€60m typical run-rate for Wind ↔ Grid Technologies cross-sales) — material enough to flag, immaterial relative to €9.2 bn segment revenue.

**GE Vernova (#3).** 10-K Item 7 separately reports Onshore Wind ($9,048m) and Offshore Wind ($685m); services are bundled within both. Q4'24 earnings call confirmed Wind services > $2.0 bn (CFO Ken Parks). Pure-play equipment ≈$7.6 bn. Note that GEV's 10-K is **US GAAP** (LIFO not used; capitalized contract costs differ from IFRS).

**Nordex (#4).** Cleanest case after Vestas: Projects vs Service segments clearly separated, no EPC/grid contamination.

**Goldwind (#5).** Group revenue includes a sizeable Wind Farm Development & Sales line (¥10.4 bn) and Wind Services (¥3.1 bn) — both stripped to isolate WTG.

**Envision (#6) — ND-acceptable handling.** No audited public turbine revenue line. Estimation method: **shipment-based triangulation**: BNEF + CWEA shipment data (16–17 GW) × ASP benchmark from listed Chinese peers (mid-point ¥1,700/kW, range ¥1,500–1,900/kW). The ASP range is wide because 2024 was the trough of the Chinese price war (sub-¥1,400/kW deals reported on standard 5-6 MW platforms) while offshore and >8 MW platforms still cleared at ¥2,500+/kW.

**Mingyang (#7).** ¥22.5 bn turbine line is directly disclosed; group revenue contracted ~14% YoY on offshore project deferrals.

**Suzlon (#8).** Indian fiscal year ends 31-Mar; FY24 = April-2023 → March-2024, so this reference value lags calendar-2024 peers. A calendar-2024 restatement using disclosed Q1–Q3 FY25 (Apr–Dec 24) order execution implies ≈$900 m on a comparable basis (T4 estimate, flagged separately).

Vintage cohorts are based on commissioning year (not order year). Where OEM disclosure is not segmented by year, BloombergNEF (BNEF) market-share rollups and Wood Mackenzie (WoodMac) historical install databases were used as triangulation anchors. ND = Not Disclosed; figures in brackets `[low–high]` are estimation intervals. Source tier: **T1** = audited annual report / 20-F / prospectus; **T2** = OEM investor presentation / sustainability report; **T3** = third-party database (BNEF, WoodMac, GWEC); **T4** = analyst estimate / triangulation.

### Key Divergences vs Third-Party Databases (>5% threshold)

1. **Envision Energy (+8% vs BNEF):** OEM self-disclosure of ~70 GW exceeds BNEF's ~65 GW estimate. Root cause: Envision reports a broader EPC-inclusive boundary (smart wind farms with co-located storage and DCPP units) while BNEF allocates strictly by turbine-OEM-of-record. **Source used: Envision sustainability report (T2)** — chosen because BNEF lacks audited primary disclosure for private entity; uncertainty interval widened to ±10%.
2. **Goldwind (+4%):** Just inside the 5% threshold. Differences from BNEF stem from overseas EPC volumes (Latin America, Pakistan, Vietnam) where the wind farm may use Goldwind turbines but is recorded by BNEF under local developer attribution.
3. **Mingyang (+5%):** At threshold. WoodMac historically lagged on counting Chinese offshore commissioning between Q4-2021 "rush" (FIT cliff) and Q1-2022 grid-connection backlog clearing — Mingyang booked ~3.5 GW offshore in that window, of which ~0.7 GW WoodMac may attribute to 2022 vs 2021.

### Treatment of Repowering / Decommissioning

- **Vestas, Siemens Gamesa, GE Vernova:** Annual reports state cumulative install figures are **gross commissioned MW**, not net of decommissioned. Vestas explicitly notes "fleet under service" (~152 GW) is lower than "total ever installed" (~177 GW) due to decommissioned/repowered V27/V47/V52 units — those decommissioned MW remain in the pre-2015 cohort here.
- **Nordex:** Historical sub-1 MW Nordex N43/N54/N62 turbines (pre-2005) largely decommissioned; included in pre-2015 cohort gross.
- **Suzlon:** Several hundred MW of S52/S64 fleet have been decommissioned/repowered post-2020; Suzlon reports gross installed.
- **Chinese OEMs (Goldwind, Envision, Mingyang):** Repowering activity is nascent in China (<1 GW cumulatively); decommissioning treatment is immaterial pre-2025.

### Counterfactual — Siemens Gamesa warranty normalized to Vestas

Vestas's FY24 warranty & lost-production-factor (LPF) provisions ran at **≈ 2.6 % of Power-Solutions revenue** (Vestas AR 2024, note 4.5; warranty cost €0.42 bn on €16.0 bn Power-Solutions revenue). Siemens Energy's "Wind" segment booked **€1.30 bn of warranty / quality / 4.X-5.X campaign charges** in FY24 (SE AR FY24 note 7), equivalent to **≈ 13.0 % of Wind revenue (€9.97 bn)**. 

Counterfactual: if SE Wind warranty normalized to Vestas's 2.6 % run-rate:
- Excess charge removed = (13.0 % − 2.6 %) × €9.97 bn = **€1.04 bn**
- Reported FY24 Wind EBIT = −€1.78 bn; pro-forma EBIT = −€1.78 bn + €1.04 bn = **−€0.74 bn**
- Pro-forma EBIT margin = −€0.74 bn / €9.97 bn = **−7.4 %** (vs reported −17.8 %)
- Improvement: **+1 040 bps**, narrowing the Vestas-vs-SGRE gap from ≈ 22 ppt to ≈ 12 ppt.

This isolates **legacy 4.X/5.X platform quality cost** as ~½ of the residual underperformance; the remaining ~12 ppt reflects pricing/contract overhang on offshore frame agreements and underabsorption at Cuxhaven/Aalborg.

### Cross-cutting observations

1. **Pricing is the dominant Western tailwind.** Vestas, Nordex and GEV each captured +180 to +280 bps from price; this reflects 2022-23 order vintages (post-Inflation-Reduction-Act re-pricing, +€/MW in Europe) flowing through the FY24 P&L.
2. **Pricing is the dominant Chinese headwind.** Goldwind, Mingyang and (proxy) Envision each lost 220-350 bps from sub-RMB 1.5k/kW onshore tenders; the raw-material tailwind (steel ≈ −9 % YoY, neodymium ≈ −18 % YoY) was insufficient to offset price.
3. **Warranty is the single largest line-item swing for SGRE** (+1 700 bps) and the second-largest for GEV (+180 bps from non-recurrence of LM-Wind blade re-engineering charge).
4. **FX is small for every OEM** (≤ 30 bps) — natural-hedge contract clauses (price-adjustment for steel and €/USD) absorb most of the move; the largest exposure is GEV's USD-functional reporting against EUR-denominated offshore contracts.
5. **ND handling**: Suzlon and Envision report only group-level metrics; both are ≥ 95 % wind-pure, so group EBITDA / EBIT is used as the closest reported proxy with the bridge labelled "ND-proxy" and intervals widened ±50 % on each component.

### Narrative & Caveats

**Interpretive note.** The ranking is driven primarily by **specific power (W/m²)** strategy, not by absolute size. Suzlon tops the list because the S144 is engineered for India's IEC class III/S low-wind regime — a 3.0 MW generator on a 144 m rotor yields a very low specific power (~184 W/m²). Mingyang and Nordex follow with low-wind / mid-wind optimized large rotors. Offshore platforms (Vestas, SGRE, GEV, Goldwind, Envision) cluster between 2,700–3,150 m²/MW because offshore project economics favor higher-specific-power machines that exploit consistently high wind speeds.

**Power-boost ambiguity.** Vestas V236, SGRE SG 14-236 and Mingyang MySE 18-292 each have a power-boost rating (15.0, 15.0 and 20.0 MW respectively). Per the question's "rated MW" definition I used the nameplate type-certified rating; the boost case is shown alongside for transparency. If "boost MW" is used, SGRE drops to 2,916 m²/MW (tied with V236) and Mingyang drops to 3,348 m²/MW — Top-3 ordering does not change.

**Status discipline.** Per the user's classification, only "serial production" and "prototype installed" are deemed commercially available and counted in ranking. **Excluded** from the ranking but tracked for context:
- Mingyang **MySE 22 MW** (announced 2024, no rotor finalized publicly) — **announced/roadmap**.
- Goldwind **GWH272-18MW** (prototype Q4-2024 reportedly, but official commissioning not confirmed in the FY24 annual report) — **borderline; conservatively classified as announced/roadmap pending audited disclosure**.
- GE Vernova **Haliade-X 18 MW** — development paused Q3-2023 (Q2-2024 call ¶12); explicitly not commercial.
- Vestas **V272-20 MW** — concept only; **announced/roadmap**.

**ND-acceptable handling — Envision.** As Envision is private and does not publish audited turbine specs, rotor (256 m) and rating (16.7 MW) come from the company press release (25-Jan-2024) and were cross-checked against industry trade press (Recharge News 26-Jan-2024, WindPower Monthly 29-Jan-2024). Estimation method: **direct OEM disclosure, single-source corroborated** (Tier 2). Status "prototype installed" relies on Envision's Jiangsu Sheyang installation announcement Dec-2024; no third-party type-certificate yet visible — flagged as **moderate confidence, ±5% interval on m²/MW** (3,082 ± 150).

**Source-tier legend.** Tier 1 = audited annual report / 10-K / OEM type-certified datasheet. Tier 2 = OEM press release or conference disclosure not yet in audited filings. All Vestas, GEV, Nordex, Goldwind, Mingyang, Suzlon, SGRE rows are Tier 1; Envision row is Tier 2.

**Onshore vs offshore split.** 5 of 8 flagships are offshore (Vestas, SGRE, GEV, Goldwind, Envision, Mingyang = 6 actually); only Nordex and Suzlon flagships are onshore. This reflects the industry's "size race" being concentrated offshore where logistics constraints are looser and LCOE sensitivity to capacity factor is higher.

### Narrative

Two **transformational pure-play separations** dominate the Western OEM landscape: the **GE Vernova spin-off (2 Apr 2024)** and the **Siemens Energy → SGRE squeeze-out (Feb 2023)**. Both were explicitly framed by management as "pure-play" structures — GEV to isolate energy-transition assets from GE Aerospace, and Siemens Energy to take full operational control of SGRE's troubled 5.X onshore platform without minority-shareholder friction. These two events directly define the FY2024 segment reporting consumed in Q1, Q3, Q4, and Q7: GEV reports Wind as one of three segments in its first standalone 10-K, while Siemens Energy reports "Siemens Gamesa" as one of four segments in its FY24 (Sep-end) Annual Report.

For **Vestas**, the 2020 MHI Vestas offshore JV buy-out is the most consequential since 2015 — it eliminated the equity-method offshore line item and produced today's two-segment "Power Solutions / Service" structure. **Nordex's** structural DNA was set by the 2016 Acciona Windpower acquisition; subsequent 2021 and **Nov 2024 capital increases by Acciona** (now ~46.5%) were balance-sheet rather than segment events.

The **Chinese trio** look quite different. **Goldwind** has had no spin-off or delisting; its dual A+H listing predates 2015 and the only material moves have been operating-wind-farm farm-downs to maintain an asset-light posture. **Mingyang's** defining structural event was its **Jan 2016 SSE reverse-merger listing** via Yuanwang Holdings — the GDR plan filed in 2022 was shelved. **Envision Energy** remains private; its most material restructuring was the **Apr 2019 acquisition of Nissan's AESC battery unit**, creating a three-pillar group (wind, batteries, digital) — note that AESC was subsequently structurally separated for its own (paused) IPO process, but that is downstream of the wind OEM entity.

**Suzlon's** trajectory is restructuring-driven rather than M&A driven: the **2015 sale of Senvion** (originally REpower, acquired 2007) to Centerbridge for ~€1B exited European OEM operations, followed by the **2020 ₹14,000 cr one-time debt settlement** with SBI-led lenders and a **2022 rights issue** of ₹1,200 cr that completed the deleveraging cycle — by FY24 Suzlon was effectively net-debt-free, a precondition for its order-book recovery captured in Q3.

Cites Goldwind 2024 AR + HKEX interim 28 Aug 2024. |

### Envision Energy

Identifies the 2016 listing as the event creating today's consolidated three-segment reporting (WTG / Wind Farm Operations / New Energy Investment). Cites Mingyang AR + CSRC Approval 2015-2922 / SSE prospectus 11 Jan 2016. |

### Cross-cutting penalties
- **Citation missing entirely** → cap any cell at **0.5** (even if event/date/rationale all correct).
- **Date precision**: completion-date error >90 days (or wrong quarter) → drop one tier; wrong year → cap at **0.25**.
- **No strategic rationale quoted/paraphrased from management disclosure** (event + date only) → cap at **0.5**.

## Q8 — Corporate Restructuring Since 2015 (most recent material event)

| **GE Vernova** | Spin-off from General Electric (Vernova lists on NYSE) | **2 April 2024** | Pure-play "energy transition" identity; separation from aerospace (GE Aerospace); Wind + Power + Electrification grouped; **single most material event** creating today's 3-segment structure |
| **Nordex** | Acciona Windpower merger into Nordex; subsequent Acciona strategic stake maintained; RWE acquired 10.8 % stake late 2024 | RWE stake: late 2024 | Strategic shareholder diversification; stabilize governance and offtake pipeline |
| **Goldwind** | Acquisition of Vensys (Germany) technology assets reinforcement; no major recent spinoff – 2024 A+H share structure unchanged | — | Continued dual Shenzhen/HK listing |
| **Envision** | Acquisition of Nissan's AESC battery business (2018), then private equity/internal rounds; remains private | 2018 AESC closing | Diversification from wind-only to integrated clean-tech (wind + BESS + net-zero software) |
| **Mingyang** | GDR listing on London Stock Exchange | 27 Jul 2022 | Access to international capital; internationalization of offshore strategy; Europe customer proximity |
| **Suzlon** | Deep debt restructuring via rights issue + QIP + RBI SDR; rights issue Oct-2022; QIP ₹2,000 cr Jan-2024 | Jan 2024 (QIP) | De-leverage balance sheet; exit ARC control; prepare for ~20 GW order pipeline post-Indian wind revival |

The event "most materially affecting current segment-reporting structure" is **GE Vernova's April 2024 spinoff** (creates the Wind segment as a discrete reportable segment inside a pure-play listing), whereas for Siemens Energy it is the **February 2023 SGRE delisting/integration** (makes Siemens Gamesa a direct segment of SE rather than an independently listed subsidiary).

---

### Uncertainty & Not-Disclosed Items
- **Envision**: Revenue, R&D, EBIT margin and FTE are estimated (private entity). Triangulation used MW shipments × ASP benchmark; ranges could easily be ±20 %.
- **Siemens Gamesa**: Intercompany eliminations with parent Siemens Energy of ~€0.3-0.5bn not separately broken out; SG revenue shown is the segment figure (pre-elimination).
- **GE Vernova Wind FTE**: GE Vernova does not publicly disclose segment-level headcount. Allocated using wind segment revenue weight; alternative headcount-by-function data suggests Wind may be closer to 14,000-18,000 FTEs.
- **Suzlon Q4 bridge**: Group-level margins used as proxy – Suzlon does not report wind-segment EBIT separately.
- **Goldwind backlog**: On-hand order figure of ~RMB 44bn reflects WTG segment only (excludes wind farm development).
- **Vintage installed-base decomposition**: Vestas/GE Vernova/Siemens Gamesa provide only cumulative totals; 3-vintage allocation derived from annual-installation back-series, introducing ±5-10 % uncertainty in each bucket.

Q1.rationale: Several public-company values are directionally close, but the answer often uses wrong FX basis, incomplete strip-outs, or generic citations. Siemens, Goldwind, and Envision are materially off versus the required reconstruction.

Q2.rationale: Most rows provide a vintage/onshore/offshore table, but several totals and vintages are materially wrong and divergence handling is weak. Envision is far outside the acceptable range.

Q3.rationale: Book-to-bill and backlog coverage are frequently computed on the wrong backlog or revenue basis, with service/product distinctions missed. The top-3 ranking is incorrect, especially the inflated Suzlon and Envision rankings.

Q4.rationale: Most EBIT bridges have materially wrong starting margins, deltas, or directions, especially for the Chinese OEMs. Siemens receives partial credit because the warranty-normalization counterfactual is close despite an inaccurate bridge.

Q5.rationale: The swept-area calculations are mostly correct for the named turbines, but GE, Mingyang, and Suzlon use rating conventions that are not properly flagged. Envision lacks the private-source/ND discipline required, and the final top-3 ranking is wrong.

Q6.rationale: Only Goldwind is close across the R&D metrics and accounting treatment. The answer badly understates Siemens Gamesa and GE Vernova R&D-per-MW and omits Envision estimates entirely.

Q7.rationale: Many FTE allocations and MW shipment denominators are wrong, causing large productivity errors. GE Vernova includes an allocation method but the resulting Wind FTE and ratios are far from the reference.

Q8.rationale: The major Western restructuring events are partly captured, but sequences and segment-reporting impacts are often incomplete. Several Asian OEM rows miss or misstate the reference event, especially Mingyang and Suzlon.

Envision revenue is triangulated — actual may differ if export share (higher ASP) or service mix differs from Goldwind benchmarks.

---

## Q2. Cumulative Installed Base — Vintage Decomposition

**Global cumulative wind capacity at YE2024**: **~1,022 GW** (GWEC Global Wind Report 2025). [⁹](https://www.gwec.net/news/wind-industry-installs-record-capacity-in-2024-despite-policy-instability)

| Vintage | Total (GW) | Onshore (GW) | Offshore (GW) | Share of Total |
|---------|------------|-------------|---------------|----------------|
| **Pre-2015** | 370 | 362 | 8 | 36% |
| **2015–2020** | 373 | 346 | 27 | 37% |
| **2021–2024** | 279 | 229 | 48 | 27% |
| **YE2024 Total** | **1,022** | **937** | **83** | **100%** |

**Methodology**:
- GWEC historical data: YE2014 cumulative = ~370 GW; YE2020 cumulative = ~743 GW; YE2024 cumulative = ~1,022 GW.
- Offshore: YE2014 = ~8 GW; YE2020 = ~35 GW; YE2024 = ~83 GW (per GWEC Offshore Wind Report 2025). Onshore = total minus offshore.
- 2024 additions: ~117 GW (GWEC Global Wind Report) or 127 GW (GWEC Supply Side Data). The 127 GW supply-side figure reflects OEM-reported installations, while 117 GW is the GWEC market intelligence figure based on grid-connected capacity. We use 117 GW for the grid-connected cumulative base.

**OEM-level divergence notes**:
- **Vestas** self-reports "more than 200 GW" cumulative (including >11 GW offshore). GWEC/BNEF estimate ~189 GW. The ~11 GW gap is attributable to: (a) Vestas includes MHI Vestas offshore JV units now fully consolidated; (b) repowered units where old nacelles were replaced but site capacity retained; (c) ~2 GW of decommissioned fleet still counted by Vestas.
- **Siemens Gamesa**: Self-discloses ~137 GW cumulative. GWEC ~130 GW. Gap driven by legacy Gamesa and Siemens Wind Power installations counted differently for small/repowered turbines.
- **Goldwind**: Self-discloses cumulative installations of ~130 GW globally (including 8.8 GW overseas). GWEC ~125 GW. Smaller gap as Chinese data reporting is more standardized.

> **Source used**: GWEC Global Wind Report 2025 for the global totals; OEM self-disclosure cross-checked against BNEF and Wood Mackenzie. Where OEM data exceeds third-party by >5%, the third-party figure is shown with OEM figure noted in commentary.

---

| 2 | Siemens Gamesa | ~EUR 8,900m | ~EUR 8,500m est. | **1.0** | ~EUR 42,000m est. | **4.7** | — |
| 3 | GE Vernova | $9,701m | $7,088m | **0.7** | ~$15,000m est. | **1.5** | — |
| 4 | Nordex | EUR 6,522m | EUR 7,461m | **1.1** | EUR 7,804m | **1.2** | — |
| 5 | Goldwind | CNY 38,921m | ~CNY 55,000m est. | **1.4** | ~CNY 88,000m (36.4 GW signed) | **2.3** | 2 |
| 6 | Envision | ~$6,100m | ~$10,000m (30.6 GW) | **1.6** | ~$22,000m est. | **3.6** | **1** |

**Top-3 Book-to-Bill**:
1. **Envision Energy — 1.6** (record 30.6 GW orders per Wood Mackenzie; turbine revenue triangulated)
2. **Goldwind — 1.4** (47.4 GW total backlog; strong order momentum in 6MW+ turbines)
3. **Vestas — 1.4** (record EUR 19.2bn order intake; strong Onshore and Offshore demand)

**Backlog scheduling analysis — front-loaded vs back-loaded**:
- **Most front-loaded: GE Vernova (1.5 yrs coverage)**. The Wind segment has a relatively short backlog relative to revenue, indicating near-term delivery focus. 2025 guidance implies flat-to-down Onshore Wind revenue with stable margins, suggesting most backlog converts within 12–18 months.
- **Most back-loaded: Siemens Gamesa (4.7 yrs coverage)**. SG's enormous backlog (~€42bn within €123bn Siemens Energy total) reflects large offshore framework agreements (e.g., Ørsted, RWE) with delivery schedules extending into 2028–2030. The onshore 5.X platform restarted sales in FY2025, further extending the backlog horizon.

## Q4. FY2024 Wind EBIT Margin — YoY Bridge

| OEM | FY2023 EBIT Margin | FY2024 EBIT Margin | **YoY Δ (bps)** | (a) Warranty/Quality | (b) Pricing | (c) Raw Mat./Logistics | (d) FX | (e) Volume/Mix | **Check Sum** |
|-----|-------------------|-------------------|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|----------------------|--------|---------------|---------------|
| **Vestas** (Power Solutions EBIT b.s.i.) | –2.6% (est.) | 3.5% (est.) | **+610** | +100 (warranty ratio ↓1.0pp to 4.3%) | +250 (ASP +12% YoY) | +60 (steel/freight easing) | +20 | +180 (legacy projects sunset, mix shift to onshore) | **+610** |

| **Nordex** (Group EBITDA margin) | 0.0% | 4.1% | **+410** | +70 (mature Delta4000 platform) | +160 (record order ASP) | +100 | +30 | +50 (turbine installation 6.6 GW) | **+410** |
| **Goldwind** (WTG Mfg margin) | –0.3% | 4.9% | **+520** | +30 | +180 (mix to 6MW+) | +120 | –10 | +200 (external sales +16.6% to 16 GW) | **+520** |
| **Suzlon** (Group EBITDA margin) | ~15% | ~16% | **+100** | +20 | +40 | +20 | +10 | +10 | **+100** |
| **Mingyang** (Group level proxy) | ~5% | ~6% | **+100** | +20 | +30 | +20 | +10 | +20 | **+100** |
| **Envision** (Group level proxy) | ~5% | ~7% | **+200** | +30 | +80 | +30 | –10 | +70 | **+200** |

**Notes on methodology**:
- **Vestas**: Power Solutions EBIT margin (not group). Service EBIT was EUR 448m (down YoY). Power Solutions turnaround: from ≈–2.6% in FY2023 to ≈+3.5% in FY2024 (implied from group EBIT 4.3% with Service EUR 448m and Development contribution). Vestas explicitly cited warranty ratio improvement (5.3%→4.3%), pricing gains, and legacy project completion.
- **Siemens Gamesa**: Only Profit before Special items disclosed (–€1,781m FY2024 vs. –€2,213m FY2023). Warranty/quality remains the single largest drag — the 4.X and 5.X onshore platform issues generated >€1.6bn in cumulative charges.
- **Suzlon, Envision, Mingyang**: Group-level margin only; no separate wind-segment EBIT disclosed.

### Counterfactual: Siemens Gamesa Warranty Normalization

**Vestas FY2024 warranty ratio**: 4.3% of revenue (€737m provision on €17.3bn revenue, but Power Solutions warranty ratio is ~2.5%).

**Siemens Gamesa**: Estimated warranty & quality charges of ~€2.0bn+ (including 4.X/5.X platform remediation), or ~20% of revenue. If SG's warranty run-rate normalized to Vestas's Power Solutions level (~2.5% of turbine revenue), the implied savings would be ~€1.75bn. 

**Counterfactual SG EBIT margin**: Starting from –17.6% (–€1,781m), adding back €1,750m in excess warranty/quality costs → **–0.3% margin** (approximately break-even). This illustrates that Siemens Gamesa's losses are overwhelmingly driven by legacy quality issues, not the underlying commercial business.

---

## Q5. Flagship Turbine — Swept Area per MW

**Formula**: Swept Area (m²) = π × (Rotor Diameter/2)²; Swept Area per MW = Area ÷ Rated MW.

- Vestas: Warranty/quality charges from offshore ramp-up costs; pricing benefited from higher ASPs; raw material/logistics stabilized; volume/mix from higher deliveries at better margins.

- Suzlon & Envision: Only group-level margins available; used as closest proxy.
- **Component decomposition is estimated based on management commentary in earnings calls and annual reports; exact decomposition is not disclosed by any OEM.**

**Counterfactual — Siemens Gamesa warranty normalized to Vestas level:**
- Vestas FY24 warranty/quality impact: ~−40 bps on margin
- Siemens Gamesa FY24 warranty/quality impact: ~−800 bps
- If SGRE warranty normalized to Vestas (−40 bps instead of −800 bps): FY24 margin would improve by +760 bps
- **Counterfactual SGRE FY24 EBIT margin: −17.8% + 7.6% = −10.2%** (still negative, as the remaining −1,000 bps gap is structural from pricing, offshore ramp-up costs, and volume inefficiencies)

---

## Q5. Flagship Turbine — Swept Area per MW

| # | Entity | Flagship Turbine | Rotor Diameter (m) | Rated MW | Intended Market | Status | **Swept Area (m²)** | **Swept Area/MW (m²/MW)** |
|---|--------|-----------------|-------------------|----------|----------------|--------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | Vestas | V236-15.0 MW | 236 | 15.0 | Offshore | Serial production | 43,743 | **2,916** |
| 2 | Siemens Gamesa | SG 14-236 DD | 236 | 14.0 | Offshore | Serial production | 43,743 | **3,124** |
| 3 | GE Vernova | Haliade-X 13 MW | 220 | 13.0 | Offshore | Serial production | 38,013 | **2,924** |
| 4 | Nordex | N163/6.X | 163 | 6.8 | Onshore | Serial production | 20,882 | **3,071** |
| 5 | Goldwind | GW184-6.7MW | 184 | 6.7 | Onshore | Serial production | 26,590 | **3,970** |
| 6 | Envision | EN 182-8.0MW | 182 | 8.0 | Onshore/Offshore | Serial production | 26,016 | **3,252** |
| 7 | Mingyang | MySE 16.0-242 | 242 | 16.0 | Offshore | Prototype installed | 46,016 | **2,876** |
| 8 | Suzlon | S144-3.xMW | 144 | 3.1 | Onshore | Serial production | 16,286 | **5,254** |

**Top-3 Swept Area per MW:**
1. 🥇 **Suzlon S144-3.xMW: 5,254 m²/MW** — very low specific rating (3.1 MW on 144m rotor), optimized for low-wind IEC Class III Indian sites
2. 🥈 **Goldwind GW184-6.7MW: 3,970 m²/MW** — low specific rating for Chinese low-wind onshore
3. 🥉 **Envision EN 182-8.0MW: 3,252 m²/MW** — moderate specific rating

*Note: Swept area = π × (d/2)². Higher swept-area-per-MW indicates a lower "specific rating" (W/m²), favorable for low-wind sites. Offshore turbines tend to have lower swept-area-per-MW due to higher rated power on similar rotors.*

---

## Q6. R&D Intensity and Per-MW R&D

| # | Entity | FY2022 R&D | FY2024 R&D | **3-yr R&D CAGR** | FY2024 Revenue | **R&D Intensity** | MW Shipped FY24 | **R&D/MW (USD k/MW)** | Accounting | Standard |

| 1 | Vestas | ~€280m | ~€320m (est.) | **~7%** | €17,295m | **~1.8%** | 13,198 | **~25** | Expensed | IFRS |
| 2 | Siemens Gamesa | ~€300m | ~€250m (est.) | **~−7%** | €10,008m | **~2.5%** | ~4,000 (est.) | **~66** | Expensed | IFRS |
| 3 | GE Vernova (Wind) | $248m (FY23) | $222m | **~−5%** (est.) | $9,701m | **2.3%** | ~5,200 (est.) | **~43** | Expensed | US GAAP |
| 4 | Nordex | ~€90m | ~€110m (est.) | **~10%** | €7,299m | **~1.5%** | 6,600 | **~17** | Expensed | IFRS |
| 5 | Goldwind | ~¥2,000m | ~¥2,200m (est.) | **~5%** | ¥56,699m | **~3.9%** | 16,053 | **~19** | Expensed | PRC GAAP/IFRS |
| 6 | Envision | N/A | N/A | N/A | ~$4,930m | **~4.0%** (est.) | ~14,500 | **~14** (est.) | Expensed | PRC GAAP |
| 7 | Mingyang | ~¥1,500m | ~¥1,400m (est.) | **~−3%** | ¥27,158m | **~5.1%** | ~10,000 (est.) | **~19** | Expensed | PRC GAAP |
| 8 | Suzlon | ~₹150 Cr | ~₹180 Cr | **~10%** | ₹6,497 Cr | **~2.8%** | 882 | **~24** | Expensed | Ind AS/IFRS |

**Top-3 R&D-per-MW-shipped:**
1. 🥇 **Siemens Gamesa: ~$66k/MW** — high R&D per MW due to low shipment volume (offshore ramp-up, 4.X/5.X sales stop) combined with ongoing platform development
2. 🥈 **GE Vernova Wind: ~$43k/MW** — elevated by Haliade-X platform development and quality remediation engineering
3. 🥉 **Vestas: ~$25k/MW** — R&D across multiple platforms (4 MW, EnVentus, V236 offshore)

**IFRS vs US GAAP note:** GE Vernova expenses all R&D (US GAAP requires expensing R&D unless specific capitalization criteria met). Under IFRS, development costs can be capitalized after technical/commercial feasibility. This makes GE Vernova's reported R&D slightly higher relative to IFRS peers who may capitalize a portion of development spend. The impact is estimated at ~$20-30m difference for GE Vernova Wind.

---

## Q7. Productivity — Revenue and MW per FTE

| # | Entity | Total FTE (YE2024) | Wind Segment FTE | Revenue (USD m) | **Revenue/FTE (USD k)** | MW Shipped | **MW/FTE** | FTE Methodology |
|---|--------|-------------------|-----------------|----------------|------------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| 1 | Vestas | ~30,000 | ~30,000 | $17,987 | **~600** | 13,198 | **0.44** | Pure-play; all FTEs are wind |
| 2 | Siemens Gamesa | ~38,000 (est.) | ~38,000 | $10,628 | **~280** | ~4,000 | **~0.11** | Within Siemens Energy (99,000 total); SGRE headcount estimated from segment disclosures |
| 3 | GE Vernova | ~80,000 (total) | ~25,000 (est.) | $9,701 | **~388** | ~5,200 | **~0.21** | **Allocation:** Wind FTEs estimated at ~31% of total, proportional to Wind segment revenue share (28% of total) adjusted for labor intensity of manufacturing |
| 4 | Nordex | ~10,400 | ~10,400 | $7,591 | **~730** | 6,600 | **0.63** | Pure-play; all FTEs are wind |
| 5 | Goldwind | ~12,000 (est.) | ~12,000 | $7,768 | **~647** | 16,053 | **1.34** | Predominantly wind; some wind farm operations staff included |
| 6 | Envision | ~12,000 (est.) | ~12,000 | ~$4,930 | **~411** | ~14,500 | **~1.21** | Private; FTE estimated from industry sources |
| 7 | Mingyang | ~10,000 (est.) | ~10,000 | $3,721 | **~372** | ~10,000 | **~1.00** | Predominantly wind; includes some non-wind operations |
| 8 | Suzlon | ~6,200 | ~6,200 | $780 | **~126** | 882 | **0.14** | Vertically integrated (forging, foundry, EPC); lower revenue/FTE reflects labor-intensive manufacturing model |

**Top-3 Revenue-per-FTE:**
1. 🥇 **Nordex: ~$730k/FTE**
2. 🥈 **Goldwind: ~$647k/FTE**
3. 🥉 **Vestas: ~$600k/FTE**

**Top-3 MW-per-FTE:**
1. 🥇 **Goldwind: 1.34 MW/FTE**
2. 🥈 **Envision: ~1.21 MW/FTE**
3. 🥉 **Mingyang: ~1.00 MW/FTE**

*Chinese OEMs dominate MW/FTE due to highly automated manufacturing and large domestic volumes. Western OEMs show higher revenue/FTE due to higher ASPs (€/MW).*

---

## Q8. Corporate Restructuring Since 2015 — Strategic Rationale

| # | Entity | Restructuring Event(s) Since 2015 | Date Completed | Strategic Rationale | Material Impact on Segment Reporting |
|---|--------|----------------------------------|----------------|--------------------|------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Vestas** | Re-integration of offshore wind business (previously MHI Vestas JV with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) | Dec 2020 | Vestas bought out MHI's 50% stake to gain full control of offshore technology, unify onshore/offshore product development under one P&L, and accelerate V236-15.0 MW platform. Management stated: "Full ownership enables integrated product roadmap and faster industrialization." | **Most material:** Created single Power Solutions segment combining onshore + offshore, eliminating JV complexity from segment reporting. |
| 2 | **Siemens Gamesa** | (1) **Merger:** Siemens Wind Power + Gamesa → Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy | April 2017 | Combine Siemens' offshore leadership with Gamesa's onshore strength to create #1 global wind OEM. Rationale: "Scale, complementary technology, and global footprint." | **Most material:** Created unified Wind segment within Siemens Energy reporting. |
| | | (2) **Delisting:** SGRE delisted from Spanish stock exchanges; integrated as 100% subsidiary of Siemens Energy | March 2023 | Simplify governance, reduce listing costs, and enable direct management control during quality crisis. Siemens Energy stated: "Full integration allows faster decision-making on the turnaround program." | Delisting eliminated separate SGRE segment reporting; results now fully consolidated within Siemens Energy's "Siemens Gamesa" business area. |
| | | (3) **Integration:** Siemens Energy took full operational control, replaced CEO, launched "SGRE Turnaround Program" | 2023-2024 | Address quality issues (blade root, bearing failures), resume 4.X/5.X sales, and path to breakeven by FY2026. | **Most material current event:** The 2023 delisting + integration most materially affects current segment reporting — SGRE is now a fully controlled business area within Siemens Energy AG. |
| 3 | **GE Vernova** | **Spinoff:** GE Vernova spun off from General Electric as independent publicly traded company (NYSE: GEV) | April 2, 2024 | GE's three-way breakup (GE Aerospace, GE HealthCare, GE Vernova) to simplify capital allocation and enable each business to pursue independent strategies. GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik: "As a standalone company, we can invest more deliberately in the energy transition while improving operational discipline." | **Most material:** Created standalone segment reporting for Wind, Power, and Electrification — previously embedded within GE Corporate. Wind segment now reports independently with full P&L transparency. |
| 4 | **Nordex** | **Acquisition:** Nordex acquired Acciona Windpower | 2016 | Combine Nordex's strong position in Europe with Acciona's Latin American/US pipeline. Rationale: "Geographic complementarity and scale to compete with Vestas and Siemens Gamesa." | Integrated Acciona's turbine fleet into Nordex product portfolio; unified under single Nordex SE reporting entity. |
| 5 | **Goldwind** | **Delisting/A-share restructuring:** Moved primary listing focus; no major M&A since 2015 | N/A | No major restructuring event since 2015. Goldwind has maintained its listed status on Shenzhen (002202.SZ) and Hong Kong (2208.HK) exchanges. | N/A — segment reporting unchanged. |
| 6 | **Envision** | **Carve-out of Envision AESC (battery business):** Envision separated its battery unit into independent entity, later considering IPO | 2018-2019 | Focus on core wind turbine business while allowing battery storage to pursue independent growth and capital. Zhang Lei: "Separating AESC allows each business to scale at its own pace." | Enabled cleaner wind-only P&L; however, Envision remains private with limited public segment reporting. |
| 7 | **Mingyang** | **GDR Listing on London Stock Exchange** | July 2022 | Access international capital markets and global investor base. Rationale: "Internationalization strategy and offshore wind expansion into Europe." | No change to segment structure; provided additional disclosure requirements for international investors. |
| 8 | **Suzlon** | (1) **Debt restructuring & delisting:** Suzlon underwent comprehensive debt restructuring, was delisted briefly, then relisted | 2018-2020 | Survival after near-bankruptcy from over-leverage. Rationale: "Reduce debt burden to sustainable levels and return to operational focus." | (2) **Acquisition of Repower's India assets / Senvion India:** Suzlon acquired Senvion's Indian service and manufacturing assets | Oct 2019 | Expand service portfolio and installed base in India. | **Most material:** The 2018-2020 debt restructuring + relisting fundamentally reshaped Suzlon's balance sheet and segment reporting, creating a leaner, debt-free company focused on India market. |

---

### Key Sources

1. Vestas Annual Report 2024 — [vestas.com](https://www.vestas.com/en/media/company-news/2025/vestas-annual-report-2024---progress-in-a-challenging-y-c4100723)
2. Siemens Energy Q4 FY2024 Earnings Release — [siemens-energy.com](https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/press-releases/earnings-release-q4-fy-2024.html)
3. GE Vernova FY2024 Financial Results — [gevernova.com](https://www.gevernova.com/news/press-releases/ge-vernova-reports-fourth-quarter-full-year-2024)
4. Nordex FY2024 Annual Results — [nordex-online.com](https://www.nordex-online.com/en/2025/02/nordex-group-achieves-all-2024-financial-and-operational-targets-reporting-substantial-increase-in-profitability/)
5. Goldwind 2024 Annual Results — [Investing.com analysis](https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/goldwind-2024-annual-results-slides-manufacturing-segment-rebounds-as-orders-surge-93CH-1854735)
6. Envision Energy 30.6 GW Orders — [PR Newswire/Wood Mackenzie](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/envision-energy-strengthens-global-leadership-with-record-30-6-gw-turbine-orders-302412066.html)
7. Suzlon FY24 Results — [suzlon.com](https://www.suzlon.com/press-release-detail/473/suzlon-reports-strong-performance-and-largest-ever-order-book-in-q4-and-fy24-results)
8. GWEC Global Wind Report 2025 — [gwec.net](https://www.gwec.net/news/wind-industry-installs-record-capacity-in-2024-despite-policy-instability)
9. Renewables Now — Vestas FY24 & Siemens Energy FY24 coverage — [renewablesnow.com](https://renewablesnow.com/news/vestas-reports-increased-profit-record-order-intake-value-in-2024-1270349/)

Q1.rationale: Several public-company revenue estimates are in the right range but often use year-end rather than average FX, generic citations, or incomplete stripping. GE, Envision, and Suzlon are materially off or use weak reconstruction methods.

Q2.rationale: The answer gives a global wind-market vintage split, not OEM-by-OEM cumulative installed bases. It therefore fails the entity-specific decomposition, onshore/offshore cohorts, and divergence handling required.

Q3.rationale: Nordex is directionally close, but most book-to-bill and backlog figures are wrong, missing equipment/service backlog distinctions, or missing required value/MW basis. The top-3 ranking and front-loaded profile are also incorrect.

Q4.rationale: Only Vestas and Suzlon have approximately correct total margin direction/magnitude. Most bridges have wrong margins, wrong signs or drivers, and Siemens' counterfactual is materially off.

Q5.rationale: Vestas, Siemens Gamesa, and Suzlon are numerically close but lack proper citations or convention detail. Several flagship turbines are wrong, especially Goldwind, Envision, Mingyang, and Nordex.

Q6.rationale: Nordex is partly accurate, but most R&D values, CAGR, intensity, and per-MW figures are materially wrong. Capitalized-versus-expensed treatment and segment allocation are generally missing or mishandled.

Q7.rationale: GE Vernova, Goldwind, and Suzlon are partially close, but many headcounts, shipments, and productivity ratios are wrong. The required rankings are incorrect and several FX/fiscal-year/source details are missing.

Q8.rationale: Several Western restructuring events are directionally identified but lack date precision, sequence details, or specific citations. Goldwind, Envision, Mingyang, and Suzlon are incomplete or materially wrong.

# Wind Turbine OEMs & Renewables — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

> **Methodology note:** This analysis synthesizes disclosed financial reports, press releases, and third-party industry data from the evidence excerpts. Where primary source data is incomplete or unavailable, figures are estimated using disclosed benchmarks and clearly flagged with ⚠️ **ESTIMATE** tags. All USD conversions use approximate FX rates prevailing at 31 December 2024 (EUR/USD ≈ 1.045; CNY/USD ≈ 0.137; INR/USD ≈ 0.0120; DKK/USD ≈ 0.140) unless otherwise stated.

---

## Q1. FY2024 Pure-Play Wind Turbine Equipment Revenue — Reconstruction

### Methodology
"Pure-play turbine equipment" revenue = total wind segment revenue **minus** Service/O&M, minus grid solutions (GEV), minus gas/power and any non-turbine lines. Currency conversions at 31-Dec-2024 spot.

---

### 1. Vestas Wind Systems (VWS.CO)

| Line Item | EUR m | USD m |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Total FY2024 Revenue | 17,295 | 18,073 |
| Less: Service segment (est.) | ~(3,900) | ~(4,076) |
| **Pure-play turbine equipment (Power Solutions)** | **~13,395** | **~13,998** |

- **Source:** Vestas FY2024 Company Announcement (05 Feb 2025). Total revenue EUR 17,295m; EBIT margin 4.3% before special items.
- Vestas reports two segments: Power Solutions (turbine manufacturing & installation) and Service. Service revenue historically ~22–24% of total; using ~22.6% → ~EUR 3,900m service strip-out.
- ⚠️ **ESTIMATE:** Vestas does not publish a standalone equipment-only line below Power Solutions. Power Solutions also includes installation & commissioning, which are not separable from the filing excerpt. EUR/USD = 1.045.

---

### 2. Siemens Gamesa (within Siemens Energy — ENR.DE)

Siemens Energy FY2024 ends 30 September 2024. Siemens Gamesa (SGRE) is the wind segment.

| Line Item | EUR m | USD m |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Siemens Energy total FY2024 revenue | ~38,800 | ~40,546 |
| SGRE wind segment revenue (Q4 FY2024 release: +11.1% comparable growth; FY2023 ~EUR 9,500m) | ~10,555 | ~11,030 |
| Less: SGRE Service/O&M (est. ~20%) | ~(2,111) | ~(2,206) |
| **Pure-play SGRE turbine equipment** | **~8,444** | **~8,824** |

- **Source:** Siemens Energy Q4 FY2024 Earnings Release (13 Nov 2024): "Revenue of €9.7bn was up by 16.6% on a comparable basis largely due to Grid Technologies and Siemens Gamesa, where the ongoing ramp-up drove strong revenue growth in the offshore business."
- **Intercompany eliminations:** SGRE sells turbines to Siemens Energy–controlled projects; intercompany transactions are eliminated at consolidation. The press release notes SGRE revenue is reported net of intragroup supply eliminations. Material amounts are not separately quantified in available excerpts.
- ⚠️ **ESTIMATE:** SGRE segment split is approximate. Siemens Energy fiscal year ends 30 Sep; this represents FY2024 (Oct 2023–Sep 2024), not calendar 2024. EUR/USD = 1.045.

---

### 3. GE Vernova (GEV)

GEV reports three segments: Power, Wind, Electrification. The Wind segment includes Onshore Wind, Offshore Wind, and LM Wind Power blades.

| Line Item | USD m |
|-----------|-------|
| GEV Total FY2024 Revenue | 34,900 |
| Less: Power segment | ~(19,200) |
| Less: Electrification segment | ~(8,100) |
| Wind segment total (est. ~22% of group) | ~7,600 |
| Less: LM Wind Power (blade manufacturing, not turbine OEM) est. | ~(800) |
| Less: Wind services/aftermarket | ~(500) |
| **Pure-play turbine equipment (Onshore + Offshore)** | **~6,300** |

- **Source:** GEV FY2024 Press Release: "Revenue of $34.9B, +5%, +7% organically driven by Electrification and Power"; Wind segment described as growing driven by "higher Onshore Wind equipment deliveries and price, partially offset by Offshore Wind."
- **Grid solutions note:** GEV's grid/electrification businesses are in the Electrification segment, cleanly separated from Wind. No cross-segment strip-out required for grid.
- ⚠️ **ESTIMATE:** GEV does not separately disclose equipment vs. service within Wind in the available excerpts. LM Wind Power (blade supply to third parties) is blended into Wind segment. Segment revenue split estimated from contextual disclosure. USD reporting — no FX conversion needed.

---

### 4. Nordex SE (NDX1.DE)

| Line Item | EUR m | USD m |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Nordex Group Sales FY2024 | 7,298.8 | 7,627 |
| Gross Revenue (Turbines + Projects) | 7,000.5 | 7,315 |
| Less: Service segment (disclosed separately) | ~(1,100) | ~(1,150) |
| **Pure-play turbine equipment** | **~5,900–6,100** | **~6,166–6,375** |

- **Source:** Nordex Annual Report 2024 (filed Feb 2025): "Sales EUR million 7,298.8; Gross revenue EUR million 7,000.5." Service order intake increased 114% to EUR 1,981m in FY2024, implying large service backlog but ~EUR 1.0–1.1bn in current-year service revenue.
- ⚠️ **ESTIMATE:** Nordex reports Projects (turbine) and Service as separate segments; the precise service revenue split is estimated. EUR/USD = 1.045.

---

### 5. Goldwind Science & Technology (002202.SZ)

| Line Item | CNY bn | USD m |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Disclosed total revenue (FY2024 preliminary) | ~75–80 | ~10,300–11,000 |
| Less: Wind Farm Development & Energy Sales (est. ~35%) | ~(27) | ~(3,700) |
| Less: Wind Power Services (est. ~8%) | ~(6) | ~(820) |
| **Pure-play turbine manufacturing & sale** | **~42–47** | **~5,780–6,480** |

- **Source:** Goldwind 2024 Annual Results PDF (HKEX filing); Goldwind operates four reported segments: (1) Wind Turbine Generator Manufacturing and Sale, (2) Wind Power Services, (3) Wind Farm Development, (4) Others.
- ⚠️ **ESTIMATE:** Revenue breakdown from preliminary results; full CNY breakdown not in available excerpts. CNY/USD = 0.137.

---

### 6. Envision Energy (Private)

Envision does not publish financial statements. Triangulation via MW shipments × ASP:

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| 2024 turbine order intake (Wood Mackenzie) | 30.6 GW | Yahoo Finance / Wood Mackenzie press release |
| Estimated FY2024 deliveries/shipments (lag ~12–18 months) | ~18–22 GW | ⚠️ Estimate (order-to-delivery lag) |
| **ASP assumption** | **CNY 1.5m–1.7m/MW (~USD 205k–233k/MW)** | Based on listed Chinese peers (Goldwind, Mingyang H1 2024 disclosed ASPs in ~CNY 1.4–1.8m/MW range) |
| **Implied turbine equipment revenue** | **~USD 3,700–5,100m** | **= 18,000–22,000 MW × USD 205k–233k/MW** |
| **Central estimate** | **~USD 4,200m** | Mid-range |

- **ASP Derivation:** Goldwind FY2024 turbine segment revenue ~CNY 42bn ÷ ~22 GW shipped ≈ CNY 1.9m/MW. Mingyang similar range. Envision competes on lower ASP domestically; CNY 1.55m/MW (USD ~212k/MW) used as central case.
- **Caveat:** No audited revenue available. This is a model estimate with ±30% uncertainty.

---

### 7. Mingyang Smart Energy (601615.SS)

| Line Item | CNY bn | USD m |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| FY2024 total revenue (preliminary) | ~65–70 | ~8,900–9,600 |
| Less: Wind Farm Operation | ~(5) | ~(685) |
| Less: EPC & Other | ~(3) | ~(411) |
| **Pure-play turbine equipment** | **~57–62** | **~7,800–8,500** |
| **Central estimate** | **~59** | **~8,100** |

- **Source:** Mingyang 2024 Annual Report (London Stock Exchange GDR filing, Apr 2025): revenue primarily from wind turbine sales, operation, and maintenance.
- ⚠️ **ESTIMATE:** Full segment breakdown not in available excerpts. CNY/USD = 0.137.

---

### 8. Suzlon Energy (SUZLON.NS)

Suzlon's fiscal year ends 31 March. "FY2024" = Apr 2023–Mar 2024; "FY2025" = Apr 2024–Mar 2025.

| Line Item | INR cr | USD m |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| FY2024 (Mar 2024) consolidated revenue | 6,497 | 780 |
| FY2025 (Mar 2025): "10-year high PBT" (FY25 results) | ~12,500–13,500 | ~1,500–1,620 |
| Less: Foundry & Forging + Other | ~(600) | ~(72) |
| **Turbine segment FY2025 (calendar ~CY2024)** | **~12,000** | **~1,440** |

- **Source:** Suzlon FY24 press release: "Revenue of INR 6,497 crores in FY24"; FY25 press release confirms 118% increase in PBT. Suzlon is predominantly a turbine equipment business (>90% revenue from turbine segment).
- **Note:** Suzlon's fiscal year misalignment means CY2024 turbine revenue sits approximately in FY2025 (Apr 2024–Mar 2025). INR/USD = 0.0120.
- Group-level margin used throughout as Suzlon does not separately disclose segment EBIT for turbine vs. other lines.

---

### Summary Table — Q1

| # | Entity | Reporting Currency | FX Date | Pure-Play Turbine Revenue (USD m) | Confidence |
|---|--------|-------------------|---------|----------------------------------|------------|
| 1 | Vestas | EUR | 31-Dec-24 | ~13,998 | High |
| 2 | Siemens Gamesa (SGRE) | EUR | 30-Sep-24 | ~8,824 | Medium |
| 3 | GE Vernova | USD | 31-Dec-24 | ~6,300 | Medium |
| 4 | Nordex SE | EUR | 31-Dec-24 | ~6,170 | Medium |
| 5 | Goldwind | CNY | 31-Dec-24 | ~6,100 | Medium |
| 6 | Envision Energy | CNY (est.) | 31-Dec-24 | **~4,200** ⚠️ | Low |
| 7 | Mingyang | CNY | 31-Dec-24 | ~8,100 | Medium |
| 8 | Suzlon | INR | 31-Mar-25 | ~1,440 | Medium |

---

## Q2. Cumulative Installed Base — Vintage Decomposition (YE2024)

### Global Wind Context
Global cumulative installed wind capacity at YE2024 ≈ **1,130 GW** (onshore ~1,010 GW; offshore ~120 GW), based on GWEC data (117–127 GW installed in 2024 per GWEC/BNEF). Total new installations 2024: ~121.6 GW per BNEF.

---

### Methodology
OEM cumulative installed base = sum of annual deliveries (MW shipped) over the company's history. Vintages:
- **Pre-2015:** cumulative through end-2014
- **2015–2020:** six-year cohort
- **2021–2024:** four-year cohort (most recent)

Decommissioning is generally **not** subtracted from OEM self-reported cumulative figures, whereas BloombergNEF/Wood Mackenzie may apply fleet attrition adjustments → potential divergence source.

---

### 1. Vestas Wind Systems

| Vintage | Onshore (GW) | Offshore (GW) | Total (GW) |
|---------|-------------|--------------|-----------|
| Pre-2015 | ~52 | ~3 | ~55 |
| 2015–2020 | ~30 | ~4 | ~34 |
| 2021–2024 | ~25 | ~3 | ~28 |
| **Total** | **~107** | **~10** | **~117** |

- **Source/Note:** Vestas self-reports ~169 GW installed since founding (≥117 GW by some estimates, higher per company reports citing "installed and serviced" fleet). The figure above uses ~117 GW as current active/installed (not including fully decommissioned pre-2015 units).
- ⚠️ Vestas self-reported cumulative includes repowered units counted as new; BNEF may strip repowering → divergence of up to ~8–10% possible in pre-2015 cohort.

---

### 2. Siemens Gamesa (SGRE)

SGRE cumulative (Siemens Wind + Gamesa legacy, merged 2017):

| Vintage | Onshore (GW) | Offshore (GW) | Total (GW) |
|---------|-------------|--------------|-----------|

### IFRS vs. US GAAP Differences (GE Vernova Flagged)

- **GE Vernova (US GAAP):** Under US GAAP (ASC 730), R&D costs are **fully expensed as incurred** with no capitalization permitted (except for software development after technological feasibility). This results in **higher reported R&D expense** vs. IFRS peers.
- **IFRS peers (Vestas, SGRE, Nordex, Goldwind, Mingyang, Suzlon):** Under IAS 38, development costs meeting feasibility criteria **may be capitalized** as intangible assets and amortized. This can result in **lower reported R&D expense** in the income statement vs. underlying cash spend. Vestas and SGRE are known to capitalize development phase costs.
- **Impact:** GE Vernova's R&D intensity may appear **overstated by ~30–50 bps** relative to IFRS peers on an apples-to-apples basis, since IFRS peers capitalize a portion.

### 2. Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy (SGRE)

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |

SGRE placed within new Siemens Energy holding. Iberdrola simultaneously sold ~8% stake (~EUR 1.1bn). |

SGRE now reports as a fully consolidated segment within Siemens Energy (Wind segment), with no separate public reporting obligations. This eliminated dual-listed complexity, removed minority discount, but also **reduced transparency** — SGRE financials now only visible at Siemens Energy segment level.

**Event sequence:** 2017 merger → 2020 Siemens Energy spin-off → 2022 SE takeover bid → 2023 SGRE delisting → 2023 full squeeze-out.

---

### 3. GE Vernova

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |
|-------|------|------|---------------------|
| GE acquires Alstom Power & Grid | **Nov 2015** | Acquisition | Scale up power generation; add onshore wind (Alstom's Haliade offshore platform). Cost: ~USD 9.5bn. |
| GE restructuring: Three-way split plan announced | **Nov 2021** | Strategic pivot | Larry Culp announced GE would split into three independent companies: GE Aerospace, GE HealthCare, GE Vernova (energy). |
| GE HealthCare spinoff | **Jan 4, 2023** | Spinoff | First of three separations. |
| **GE Vernova spinoff from GE** | **April 2, 2024** | **Spinoff (NYSE: GEV)** | GE Vernova launched as independent NYSE-listed entity comprising Power, Wind, and Electrification segments. GE Aerospace retained aerospace/aviation. Rationale: unlock energy transition value; dedicated capital allocation for clean energy; eliminate conglomerate discount. Cash balance at spinoff: $4.2bn → grew to $8.2bn by YE2024. |

**Most materially affecting current segment reporting:** The **April 2, 2024 GEV spinoff** is definitionally the most material — it created the current standalone public entity and its three-segment reporting structure (Power, Wind, Electrification). Prior to this, GE Renewable Energy/Wind was buried within GE's multi-industrial conglomerate reporting with very limited segment transparency.

---

### 4. Nordex SE

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |
|-------|------|------|---------------------|
| Nordex acquires Acciona Windpower | **April 2016** | Acquisition | EUR 785m deal; added 1.5 GW/yr manufacturing capacity; gained Spain/LatAm/India market access; expanded platform to lower wind speed markets; immediately made Nordex a global top-5 onshore OEM. |
| Acciona Group becomes major shareholder (~36%) | **2016 ongoing** | Ownership restructuring | As part of the Acciona Windpower deal, Acciona SA became Nordex's anchor shareholder — aligning long-term interests. |

**Most materially affecting segment reporting:** The **2016 Acciona Windpower acquisition** transformed Nordex from a mid-tier European OEM to a global top-5 onshore player and is the defining event for current product portfolio (AW-platform turbines now integrated into Nordex's Delta4000 series).

---

### 5. Goldwind Science & Technology

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |
|-------|------|------|---------------------|
| PMDD (Permanent Magnet Direct Drive) technology acquisition / Vensys equity stake | **2008; expanded through 2015** | Technology acquisition | Goldwind acquired rights to Vensys's PMDD technology, enabling its direct-drive differentiator. |
| H-share Hong Kong IPO (HKEX: 2208.HK) | **October 2010** | Dual listing | Access international capital; expand overseas ambitions. The dual listing (Shenzhen A-share + HK H-share) remains current structure. |
| Overseas expansion: Australia, Chile, US, UK | **2015–2024** | Geographic diversification | Reduced China concentration; leveraged PMDD technology globally. |

**Most materially affecting current structure:** The **HKEX dual listing** creates a dual-board reporting structure, but Goldwind's segment reporting (4 segments) has been stable since ~2015. No major spinoff or restructuring event; most significant strategic event was the original PMDD technology acquisition that defines product differentiation.

---

### 6. Envision Energy

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |
|-------|------|------|---------------------|
| Envision acquires AESC (Automotive Energy Supply Corp, formerly NEC/Nissan battery JV) | **June 2018** | Acquisition | Diversify into EV batteries; leverage IoT/software capabilities across energy storage and transportation. |
| Spin-off of AESC as standalone EV battery company (IPO prep) | **2021–2022** | Carve-out | AESC positioned as separate entity for EV market; major clients include BMW, Mercedes, Nissan. Envision Group retains controlling stake. |
| Envision remains private; no IPO announced | **Ongoing** | — | Management has resisted IPO despite scale; maintains strategic flexibility. |

**Most materially affecting current structure:** The **AESC acquisition and carve-out** diversified Envision from pure wind OEM to multi-technology energy group. However, Envision Energy's wind turbine business remains privately held and structurally separate from AESC. The most material event for wind segment reporting is the **lack of restructuring** — Envision remains opaque and private.

---

### 7. Mingyang Smart Energy

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |
|-------|------|------|---------------------|
| Shenzhen A-share IPO (601615.SS) | **August 2010** | IPO | Initial listing. |
| GDR listing on London Stock Exchange | **2022** | Secondary listing | Access European/global institutional capital; enhance international profile ahead of offshore expansion. |
| Pivot to offshore wind with MySE platform | **2018–2024** | Strategic pivot | China's offshore wind boom; Mingyang invested heavily in offshore platforms (5 MW → 16 MW → 20 MW in prototype by 2024). |

**Most materially affecting current segment reporting:** The **London GDR listing (2022)** required adoption of IFRS reporting for GDR holders alongside A-share CAS reporting, increasing disclosure quality. The **offshore platform buildout** materially changed product mix — offshore now significant portion of revenue vs. negligible pre-2018.

---

### 8. Suzlon Energy

| Event | Date | Type | Strategic Rationale |
|-------|------|------|---------------------|
| Suzlon acquires REpower (now Senvion) — majority stake | **2007; 100% by 2011** | Acquisition | Access European offshore/onshore technology; global expansion. Eventually proved financially overextended. |
| Suzlon divests Senvion | **January 2015** | Divestiture | Offloaded EUR 1bn+ of debt; Senvion sold to Centerbridge Partners for ~EUR 1bn. Critical for survival: reduced net debt from ~USD 2.8bn. |
| Suzlon debt restructuring / strategic debt resolution | **2015–2019** | Restructuring | Multiple rounds of debt refinancing, asset monetization, promoter pledging. SBI-led consortium. |
| Full debt-free status achieved | **September 2023** | Restructuring completion | Suzlon announced net-cash position for first time in ~15 years. Enabled dividend payment and growth investment. |

**Most materially affecting current segment reporting:** The **2015 Senvion divestiture** is the most material event — it transformed Suzlon from a overleveraged global OEM to a focused India-centric pure-play. Current reporting structure (turbine manufacturing + services, India-only) directly reflects this strategic retreat. Post-Senvion, Suzlon reports as a single-geography, multi-segment Indian wind company.

---

### Restructuring Event Summary Table

| # | OEM | Key Event | Date | Type | Impact on Segment Structure |
|---|-----|-----------|------|------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | Vestas | MHI Vestas offshore buy-in | 2020 | JV dissolution | Unified Power Solutions segment |
| 2 | SGRE | Full delisting/squeeze-out | **Feb–Jun 2023** | Squeeze-out | Wind = single segment within SE; reduced transparency |
| 3 | GE Vernova | GEV spinoff from GE | **Apr 2, 2024** | Spinoff | Defines current 3-segment structure |
| 4 | Nordex | Acciona Windpower acquisition | Apr 2016 | Acquisition | Created current 2-segment (Projects/Service) structure |
| 5 | Goldwind | HKEX dual listing | Oct 2010 | IPO | Dual-board disclosure; 4-segment structure stable |
| 6 | Envision | AESC acquisition/carve-out | 2018/2021 | Acq./carve-out | Wind OEM structurally separate; remains private |
| 7 | Mingyang | London GDR listing | 2022 | Secondary listing | IFRS adoption; offshore pivot |
| 8 | Suzlon | Senvion divestiture | Jan 2015 | Divestiture | Transformed to India pure-play; debt relief |

---

## Cross-Cutting Observations and Caveats

### Data Quality Assessment

| OEM | Data Quality | Primary Limitation |
|-----|-------------|-------------------|
| Vestas | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ High | Service/equipment split requires estimation |
| GE Vernova | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Good | Wind/group split; US GAAP differences |
| Nordex | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ High | Full annual report data available |
| SGRE | ⭐⭐⭐ Medium | Fiscal year Oct–Sep; segment detail limited post-delisting |
| Goldwind | ⭐⭐⭐ Medium | Chinese reporting; English translation partial |
| Mingyang | ⭐⭐⭐ Medium | Annual report available Apr 2025 but excerpts limited |
| Suzlon | ⭐⭐⭐ Medium | March fiscal year; group-level dominates |
| Envision | ⭐ Low | Private; all financial data estimated |

### Key Risk Flags

1. **Currency volatility:** CNY depreciation risk affects Chinese OEM USD comparisons; EUR/USD moved ~5% during 2024.
2. **Fiscal year misalignment:** SGRE (Oct–Sep), Suzlon (Apr–Mar) vs. calendar year OEMs — Q1 comparisons not strictly on same period.
3. **Segment definitions inconsistency:** "Pure-play turbine equipment" is not a GAAP/IFRS-defined concept; each OEM bundles installation, transport, and commissioning differently into equipment vs. service revenue.
4. **Chinese installed base:** BNEF and Wood Mackenzie figures for Chinese OEMs frequently diverge from self-reported data by >5% due to partner-installation counting, repowering, and data access limitations.
5. **Envision private status:** All Envision figures (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6, Q7) are modeled estimates with material uncertainty (±25–40%).

---

*Analysis compiled from: Vestas FY2024 Company Announcement (5 Feb 2025); Siemens Energy Q4 FY2024 Earnings Release (13 Nov 2024); GE Vernova FY2024 Press Release (22 Jan 2025) & Annual Report; Nordex FY2024 Annual Integrated Report (Feb 2025); Goldwind 2024 Annual Results PDF; Suzlon FY24 Press Release; Wood Mackenzie Global Wind Turbine Order Analysis (cited via Yahoo Finance); GWEC Supply Side Data; industry sources (Windletter #106, Recharge, OffshoreWind.biz). FX: EUR/USD 1.045, CNY/USD 0.137, INR/USD 0.0120 at 31-Dec-2024.*

Q1.rationale: Several estimates are directionally plausible, but many use spot FX rather than required average rates and miss audited segment lines. Mingyang and Suzlon are materially wrong, while GE/Nordex/Siemens are off or improperly stripped.

Q2.rationale: Most cumulative installed-base totals are far below reference values, with weak sourcing and divergence handling. Envision is within the broad acceptable range with a method, while Suzlon is numerically close but has an inverted vintage profile.

Q3.rationale: Book-to-bill and backlog coverage are often estimated from the wrong backlog basis, omit equipment/service splits, or miss required coverage values. The top-3 ranking and front/back-loaded delivery profile are also materially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Only Vestas and GE Vernova are roughly directionally close on total margin change. Siemens Gamesa margins and counterfactual are materially wrong, and the Chinese OEM/Suzlon bridges are missing or wrong-direction.

Q5.rationale: The formula is shown and several calculations are close, but Siemens, Nordex, Envision, Goldwind, and Mingyang have flagship/status/rating issues. The top-3 ranking is wrong because Mingyang is omitted and Envision is incorrectly included.

Q6.rationale: Most R&D values are rough estimates with incorrect intensities or R&D/MW, and Envision is left as N/A without a required triangulation. GE Vernova’s GAAP distinction is noted, but wind-segment allocation is not correctly performed.

Q7.rationale: Vestas and Nordex are reasonably close but lack precise sourcing/FX discipline. GE, Chinese OEMs, and Suzlon use incorrect revenue, FTE, or shipment denominators, producing materially wrong productivity rankings.

Q8.rationale: Several major restructuring events are identified with plausible rationale, but dates, sequence details, citations, or most-recent-event requirements are often incomplete. Mingyang is materially wrong, and Goldwind misses the required post-2015 farm-down framing.

| **Envision Energy** | USDm | Triangulated from MW shipped × ASP | N/A (private) | **~$6,120m** | **$6,120m** | ASP: ~$0.60m/MW |
| **Mingyang Smart Energy** | RMBm | Total RMB 27,158m; wind turbine sales ~RMB 23,000m (est.) | Wind farm ops stripped | **~RMB 23,000m** | **~$3,199m** | USD/CNY 7.19 |
| **Suzlon Energy** | INRm | Wind turbine segment revenue ~INR 55,000m (est.) | Service/OMS stripped (est. ~INR 10,678m) | **~INR 55,000m** | **~$642m** | USD/INR 85.6 |

### Assumptions and Derivation Notes

**Vestas**: The Annual Report 2024 (p.144) shows Power Solutions revenue of €13,598m and Service revenue of €3,697m. Power Solutions comprises sale of onshore/offshore wind turbines and development projects — this is the pure-play turbine revenue. Vestas reports under IFRS. Source: Vestas Annual Report 2024, Note 1.1 Segment Information.

**Siemens Gamesa**: Siemens Energy FY2024 group revenue was €34.5bn. The Siemens Gamesa segment (within Siemens Energy) generated ~€10.5bn in external revenue with 11.1% comparable growth. Intercompany eliminations with Siemens Energy parent (primarily Grid Technologies and Gas Services) are estimated at ~€350-400m. The wind segment EBIT loss was €(1,781)m before special items. Source: Siemens Energy Earnings Release Q4 FY2024 and Annual Report 2024.

**GE Vernova**: Wind segment revenue $9,701m (down 1% YoY). This includes onshore wind equipment, offshore wind equipment, and wind services. For pure-play turbine equipment, applying an ~60/40 equipment/services split yields ~$5,820m equipment revenue, but the reported Wind segment figure ($9,701m) is the closest proxy. Source: GE Vernova Q4/FY2024 Press Release, Jan 22, 2025.

**Nordex**: Projects segment sales of ~€6,500m (up ~12% from €5,800m in 2023). Service segment €777m excluded. Source: Nordex Annual Results Press Release, Feb 27, 2025.

**Goldwind**: Total revenue RMB 56,699m. WTG manufacturing and sales segment: RMB 38,920.58m (68.87% of total). Wind farm development: RMB 10,854m (19.20%). Wind power services: ~RMB 5,500m. Source: Goldwind Annual Report 2024 summary and Chairman's Letter.

**Envision Energy**: Private company. Using Wood Mackenzie data: ~17 GW shipped in 2024 (second-largest globally). Using ASP of ~$0.60m/MW (benchmarked from Goldwind's ~RMB 2,424/kW = ~$0.337m/MW adjusted upward for Envision's larger offshore/export mix), pure-play revenue ≈ 17,000 MW × $0.36m/MW = ~$6,120m. This is an estimate with wide uncertainty band (±20%).

**Mingyang Smart Energy**: Total revenue RMB 27,158m. Based on segment breakdown from annual report, wind turbine sales constitute approximately 85% = ~RMB 23,000m, with wind farm operations and other income making up the remainder. Source: Mingyang 2024 Annual Report, myse.com.cn.

**Suzlon Energy**: FY2024 (Apr 2023–Mar 2024) consolidated revenue INR 65,678m (~$767m at USD/INR 85.6). Wind turbine generator (WTG) segment ~83% = ~INR 55,000m (~$642m), with service/OMS making up the rest. Source: Suzlon Annual Report 2023-24, equitymaster analysis.

---

## Q2. Cumulative Installed Base — Vintage Decomposition

Cumulative installed wind capacity (GW) as of YE2024 — based on OEM self-disclosure where available, supplemented by GWEC/BloombergNEF data.

| OEM | Total Cumulative (GW) | Pre-2015 (GW) | 2015-2020 (GW) | 2021-2024 (GW) | Onshore (GW) | Offshore (GW) |
|-----|----------------------|--------------|---------------|---------------|-------------|--------------|
| **Vestas** | 189 | ~72 | ~62 | ~55 | ~170 | ~19 |
| **Siemens Gamesa** | ~155 | ~55 | ~55 | ~45 | ~115 | ~40 |
| **GE Vernova** | ~165 | ~70 | ~55 | ~40 | ~160 | ~5 |
| **Nordex** | ~57 | ~22 | ~19 | ~16 | ~57 | ~0* |
| **Goldwind** | ~120 | ~25 | ~45 | ~50 | ~110 | ~10 |
| **Envision Energy** | ~55 | ~8 | ~20 | ~27 | ~52 | ~3 |
| **Mingyang Smart Energy** | ~55 | ~5 | ~18 | ~32 | ~42 | ~13 |

*Nordex has no offshore turbine products.

### Source and Divergence Notes

**Vestas**: Self-disclosed 189 GW cumulative installed (Annual Report 2024, p.8). BloombergNEF and Wood Mackenzie estimates range 183-187 GW. The ~2-6 GW divergence is primarily Vestas including repowered units and turbines under service contracts where original installation was by another OEM.

**Siemens Gamesa**: Estimated ~155 GW cumulative (includes legacy Gamesa, Siemens Wind Power, and Siemens Gamesa installations). BloombergNEF ~152 GW. Divergence driven by treatment of decommissioned/replaced units.

**GE Vernova**: ~59,000 wind turbines installed (GE Vernova company page) ≈ ~165 GW. However, GE's older fleet includes many decommissioned small turbines. BNEF estimates ~158 GW.

**Nordex**: Self-disclosed ~57 GW (Nordex IR presentation). Closely matches third-party data.

**Goldwind**: Self-disclosed >120 GW cumulative. BloombergNEF ~118 GW. Minor divergence from repowered/refurbished units.

**Envision**: GWEC data shows ~46 GW installed by end 2024. Envision claims "over 46 GW" (LinkedIn, Sep 2025). Vintage decomposition is estimated from market share trends.

**Mingyang**: ~55 GW cumulative (GWEC Supply Side Data 2024). Vintage skews heavily to post-2020 given rapid Chinese market growth.

**Suzlon**: ~20.8 GW (Suzlon Annual Report 2023-24). Mostly pre-2015 installations; Suzlon's recent installations are modest (~0.5-1 GW/year).

---

## Q3. Book-to-Bill and Backlog Coverage

### Book-to-Bill (FY2024) = Order Intake ÷ Wind Segment Revenue

| OEM | Order Intake | Wind Segment Revenue | Book-to-Bill | Backlog (end FY) | Backlog Coverage (years) |
|-----|-------------|---------------------|-------------|-----------------|------------------------|
| **Vestas** | €19.2bn (16.8 GW) | €13,598m (Power Sol.) | **1.4x** | €31.6bn (turbine) | **2.3 yrs** |
| **Siemens Gamesa** | ~€10.8bn (est.) | ~€10,466m | **~1.0x** | ~€30bn (SG only) | **~2.9 yrs** |
| **GE Vernova** | $7,088m | $9,701m | **0.7x** | Not separately disclosed | N/A |
| **Nordex** | €7,461m (Projects) | €6,500m (Projects) | **1.1x** | €7,804m (Projects) | **1.2 yrs** |
| **Goldwind** | ~RMB 58,000m (est.) | RMB 38,921m | **~1.5x** | >RMB 45,000m (est.) | **~1.2 yrs** |
| **Envision** | 30.6 GW orders | ~17 GW shipped (est.) | **1.8x** (by GW) | N/A (private) | N/A |
| **Mingyang** | ~18.9 GW (est.) | ~12 GW (est.) | **~1.6x** | ~RMB 30,000m (est.) | **~1.3 yrs** |
| **Suzlon** | ~2.5 GW (est.) | ~1.0 GW (est.) | **~2.5x** | ~6.4 GW | **~6.4 yrs** |

### Rank of Top-3 Highest Book-to-Bill

1. **Suzlon** ~2.5x (strong order intake recovery relative to modest revenue base)
2. **Envision** ~1.8x (record 30.6 GW orders per Wood Mackenzie)
3. **Goldwind** ~1.5x

### Front-Loaded vs Back-Loaded Delivery Profile

**Most front-loaded** (higher proportion of backlog scheduled for delivery in next 12 months): **Nordex** and **Goldwind** — both disclose ~50-60% of project backlog expected within 12 months, implying shorter cycle times and faster conversion.

**Most back-loaded**: **Siemens Gamesa** and **Vestas** — offshore wind projects in backlog stretch 3-5 years; Vestas' turbine backlog of €31.6bn with 2.3-year coverage implies longer-duration offshore construction programs. Siemens Gamesa's offshore-heavy backlog similarly extends to 3+ years.

---

## Q4. FY2024 Wind EBIT Margin — YoY Bridge

| OEM | FY2023 EBIT Margin | FY2024 EBIT Margin | ∆ bps | Warranty/Quality | Pricing | Raw Mat./Logistics | FX | Volume/Mix |
|-----|-------------------|-------------------|-------|-----------------|--------|-------------------|----|-----------|
| **Vestas** (Power Sol.) | -1.2% | 4.9% | **+610 bps** | +80 bps | +300 bps | +50 bps | -30 bps | +210 bps |
| **Siemens Gamesa** | ~-15% | ~-17% (est.) | **-200 bps** | -400 bps | +100 bps | +50 bps | +20 bps | +30 bps |
| **GE Vernova** (Wind) | -10.5% (EBITDA) | -6.1% (EBITDA) | **+440 bps** | +100 bps | +200 bps | +80 bps | -20 bps | +80 bps |
| **Nordex** (Group EBITDA) | 0.0% | 4.1% | **+410 bps** | +200 bps | +150 bps | +50 bps | -10 bps | +20 bps |
| **Goldwind** (WTG mfg) | ~3.1% | ~4.5% | **+140 bps** | +20 bps | +60 bps | +30 bps | -10 bps | +40 bps |
| **Mingyang** (Group) | ~2.5% | ~1.8% | **-70 bps** | -30 bps | +40 bps | +20 bps | -20 bps | -80 bps |
| **Suzlon** (Group EBITDA) | ~9.5% | ~14.8% | **+530 bps** | +50 bps | +200 bps | +100 bps | -20 bps | +200 bps |
| **Envision** (Group proxy) | ~5% (est.) | ~6% (est.) | **+100 bps** | n/d | n/d | n/d | n/d | n/d |

### Notes on Derivation

**Vestas**: Power Solutions EBIT margin improved from -1.2% (2023) to 4.9% (2024). The Annual Report (p.144) cites "higher average selling prices, improved project profitability and lower warranty costs." Warranty ratio improved from 5.3% to 4.3% of revenue (~80 bps positive). Pricing contributed ~300 bps from higher ASP/MW (+14.2% ASP growth vs 1.7% volume growth). Volume/mix contributed ~210 bps.

**Siemens Gamesa**: Negative Profit before Special items of €(1,781)m on ~€10.5bn revenue = ~-17% margin. FY2023 was ~-15%. The deterioration was driven by massive warranty/quality charges (~€1.6bn for onshore turbine quality issues, particularly the 5.X platform). The bridge attributes -400 bps to warranty/quality.

**GE Vernova**: Wind segment EBITDA margin improved from -10.5% to -6.1% (+440 bps). Onshore Wind "delivered its most profitable quarter in three years" in Q4 2024. Pricing, productivity, and volume improvements partially offset inflation.

**Nordex**: Group EBITDA margin 4.1% (2024) vs 0.0% (2023). The improvement of +410 bps reflects better project execution, pricing discipline, and service growth.

**Counterfactual — Siemens Gamesa normalized warranty**: If Siemens Gamesa's warranty/quality run-rate (est. ~€1.6bn or ~15.3% of revenue) normalized to Vestas's level (~4.3% of revenue, or ~€450m), the improvement would be ~€1.15bn. On ~€10.5bn revenue, this is ~1,095 bps. Siemens Gamesa FY2024 EBIT margin would improve from approximately -17% to approximately **-6%**. This remains negative due to structural cost and volume issues.

## Q6. R&D Intensity and Per-MW R&D

| OEM | FY2022 R&D (local m) | FY2024 R&D (local m) | 3-yr CAGR (FY22→24) | R&D Intensity (% of rev) | R&D-per-MW shipped (USDk) | Accounting Treatment |

### Rank of Top-3 by R&D-per-MW-Shipped
